problem: Listing photos were poor, which they thought hurt bookings.
title: Airbnb's founders photograph hosts' listings themselves in New York
context: Airbnb was struggling in 2009, with weak bookings in New York.
decision_made: Rent a camera and take professional-quality photos of hosts' listings themselves, doing things that do not scale.
action_taken: Visited hosts in person, and later turned it into an Airbnb Photography programme in 2010.
observed_outcome: Accounts say New York revenue roughly doubled after the photos. One blog said weekly revenue went from $200 to $400. Paul Graham noted that the visits also taught them about their hosts.
lessons: Doing unscalable manual work early can reveal what customers need and prove a hypothesis cheaply.
limitations: Revenue figures come from retellings and blogs, and camera cost is reported as $500 or $5,000. A later university study reported by a secondary source was not read. Survivorship bias applies.

claims.claim_text: Gebbia and Chesky rented a professional camera and photographed hosts' places themselves.
Accounts say Airbnb's New York revenue roughly doubled after the professional photos.
